sections.h2: Who sends an Independence property tax bill
sections.html:
The City of Independence does not bill real estate tax. Jackson County does, through two departments: Assessment sets the value, and Collection mails the bill and takes the money. Independence owners can pay at the Historic Truman Courthouse, 112 W Lexington Ave, Suite 114, or at the Jackson County Courthouse in Kansas City. Both open at 8:00 a.m. and close at 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, except county holidays.

Collection answers at (816) 881-3232 and Collections@jacksongov.org. To fix a name or mailing address on a real property account, phone Assessment at 816-881-3530. A change of address filed with the post office or the Missouri DMV never reaches the tax account. Phone lines run long in November and December, so email or the online account lookup may be quicker for simple questions.

The tax year 2026 deadline is December 31, 2026. In the prior cycle the county printed bills in early November and finished mailing on December 12. Owners with no bill by December 8 are told to call, and the county warns that a bill that never came is no defense. A check needs a USPS postmark dated December 31 or earlier. The county suggests mailing days early because post office drop boxes sometimes stamp the next day.

The drop box at the south door of the Truman Courthouse locks at midnight on the last day, and cash does not belong in it. Extra Saturday morning hours were offered before the 2025 deadline, so check the Collection page for any new schedule.

Jackson County online payment charges
Payment typeCharge
Any online payment$2.00 flat
E-check (ACH)plus $1.25
Debit or credit cardplus 2.75%
Check or money orderMade out to Jackson County Collector, with the account number

The county says it keeps none of these charges, which go to the payment processor. The online system stops at 11:40 p.m. on December 31.

sections.h2: How a sale affects the bill
sections.html:
Jackson County treats the tax as a lien that follows the real estate, so a buyer inherits any unpaid real estate tax. Buyer and seller commonly prorate the year at closing, and a closing company may pay whatever is due if it knows the amount. As a rule nobody pays the Collector on the day of sale.

  • A buyer who gets a credit at closing should confirm it is meant for the coming tax bill.
  • The new bill may still go out in the seller's name until the buyer reports ownership and an address to the Assessor.
  • Homes with escrow accounts need the bill forwarded to the lender.

Check the parcel at payments.jacksongov.org before you list. Prior-year balances land on the current statement as one lump, so keep last year's bill if you need the breakdown.

The Board of Equalization accepts filings from May 1 through mid-July each year. After that the window is shut until the next cycle. The Board meets at 1300 Washington in Kansas City, and owners who have filed can withdraw in writing at any time.

Appeals for 2026 will not change this year's statement. Jackson County says recalculation of 2026 appeals and stipulations is paused until January 2027, so pay the full 2026 amount by December 31, 2026. Any overpayment comes back as an automatic refund, with no protest needed. Partial payments on real estate are accepted but cannot be made online, and interest and fees still apply to the unpaid remainder.

The State Tax Commission is the next level and runs its own online application. An owner who signed the Assessor's stipulation has closed the Board case and cannot go on to the Commission.

Independence sits on the south bank of the Missouri River, mostly in Jackson County with a small piece in Clay County. The 2020 census counted 123,011 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 121,675. There are 51,477 households, 60.9 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the median owned home is valued at $172,900, median gross rent is $1,109 and median household income is $60,339.

Independence, Blue Springs, Fort Osage and Raytown each have school district territory inside the city, so buyers ask which district a particular street falls under. The parcel record answers that.

Where a charter county's valuation came from a computer-assisted method, RSMo 137.115 says the assessor must back it with appraisal-based findings and the prices of at least three comparable sales within a mile.

If you expect to challenge a value later, start collecting your own proof now. The Board's appeal page lists certified appraisals, sale contracts and settlement statements, repair estimates and, for income property, rent rolls and leases. A real estate agent's opinion does not qualify, and evidence shown on a phone or tablet will not be considered at the hearing.

sections.h2: If you are paying close to the deadline
sections.html:
Order matters in the last week of December. An online payment is the fastest proof, since the system runs until 11:40 p.m. on December 31 and you can print what you paid. A mailed check is judged by its postmark, and the post office is the weak point, because a drop box can stamp the next day. In person, the Truman Courthouse counter closes at 5:00 p.m., while the drop box stays open until midnight but is no place for cash.

Lines at the counter and on the phone are longest in November and December, so people who only need to confirm a balance or print a statement are better off using the account lookup or sending an email to Collections@jacksongov.org.

If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, the bill still needs to reach the lender, and a seller should not assume that happened on its own. Send the statement on, or ask the servicer to confirm it has the current bill. After a sale, the buyer's lender will want the same document, so keep a copy.

A buyer who receives a credit at closing for the seller's share should check that the money is set aside for the coming bill. Since the new bill may still be addressed to the seller, the buyer should report ownership and a mailing address to Assessment rather than wait for the county to catch up.

sections.h2: Selling an Independence house with tax questions
sections.html:
Phone Collection at (816) 881-3232 and ask whether any prior year is open on your parcel. Tell Assessment at 816-881-3530 if the owner's name or mailing address needs correcting, since the post office and the DMV will not pass that along. Give the title company the current statement so it can prorate the year.

If a lien, a tenant or a repair list is slowing a conventional sale, a cash buyer can close without a lender's appraisal, and the tax balance is paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Which office collects Independence property tax?
faqs.a: Jackson County's Collection Department, at the Historic Truman Courthouse in Independence or the Kansas City courthouse. Call (816) 881-3232.

faqs.q: What is the payment deadline for tax year 2026?
faqs.a: December 31, 2026. Mailed payments need that postmark or an earlier one, and the online system accepts payments until 11:40 p.m. that night.

faqs.q: Do buyers or sellers settle the Independence tax bill?
faqs.a: They usually prorate the year at closing, and a closing company may pay any amount already due. The buyer is liable for unpaid real estate tax because it follows the property.

faqs.q: Can a pending appeal lower the 2026 bill before it is due?
faqs.a: No. Recalculations are suspended until January 2027, so pay the whole 2026 bill by December 31 and a refund follows automatically if the value drops.

faqs.q: What fee applies to online tax payments in Independence?
faqs.a: A $2.00 fee per transaction, plus $1.25 for e-checks or 2.75 percent for cards. The county says it receives none of these fees.
